chapter: Silvers, Rampart Street and Army service
title: Studying at Xavier before the Army
summary: He spent almost two years at Xavier in general courses toward medicine, drawn away by thoughts of the Army, girls and his sick mother.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: So, did you go to Xavier before you went in the Army?

Yeah, yeah, yeah. See, I didn't go into Fortitude, and I spent about a year and a half, I'd say, almost two years, yeah, just about two years. And then I went into the service, you know, I always could read or write real good, could count good, things like that. And then I was energetic, and I'm tall, and I could run fast, I was a good athlete, then I could always shoot, because I, look, even today, I'm a marksman, perfect marksman. And when they put me out on the firing range, see I knew how to hold my breath, I knew how to breathe. My grandfather taught me a lot of stuff before I went into the service. It's just like my mother, my father, I don't ever remember my father reprimanding me, just talk to me, but my mother was the one who really could tear up a behind boy. Really, my mother could really put your lights out.
When you went to Xavier, what did you study at Xavier?
What was your job? I started as just a general student. Like I said, I wanted to be a doctor, so what I started was just taking general courses leading up to that.
So you didn't have a specialty?
